node_model.note: BASIS/family labels are metadata for inspection, not execution layers.

edge_semantics.calls: Tactic -> SOP. Declares the SOP vocabulary that a tactic may compose. It is not a mandatory linear order.
edge_semantics.jump: Tactic -> Tactic or SOP -> SOP. A legal handoff that may be default-sequenced or context-triggered. No provider/tool edge is part of the scientific graph.

state_semantics.skill_behavior: consume a relevant state slice and return a research-state delta; never require provider-specific storage or giant checkpoint files.

tactics.desc: Rank, classify, screen, or select typed candidates under explicit criteria and supplied hard constraints. Object schema and decision mode are parameters; pairwise and portfolio cases may jump to dedicated tactics.
old: present-and-ask [dialogue sop; interaction moved to runtime]
tactics.why: The three tactics share the same criteria→score→aggregate kernel. Their differences are object schema and optional preconditions, not a different scientific transformation. Pairwise active comparison and portfolio subset optimization remain separate tactics because their state/update logic differs.

tactics.desc: Map where a claim, method, or design remains valid by defining variation axes, probing systematic or adversarial/boundary values, detecting breakpoints, and constructing a multidimensional validity envelope. Critical-case selection is an optional inference-maximizing mode.
tactics.why: Deep-insight and stress-test both encoded validity-envelope mapping with the same output and nearly identical breakpoint/envelope operations. Boundary stress is an extreme-value sampling policy over the same workflow, not a separate algorithm.

tactics.desc: Represent a problem/research space as validated dimensions and values, enumerate compatible combinations, and optionally map occupancy, detect gaps, prioritize regions, or synthesize candidate questions/ideas.
tactics.why: Both tactics operate on the same dimension×value combinatorial representation and share enumeration plus compatibility checking. Research-space mapping adds occupancy/gap analysis as a downstream mode; it does not require a distinct kernel.

tactics.desc: Run structured attack/defense/adjudication over a claim, candidate, criterion set, or current winner. Perspective, target, escalation depth, loser-resurrection, and steelman/winner-stress modes are parameters; role execution is runtime-agnostic.
tactics.why: Both tactics use the same critique→defense→adjudication kernel. Steel-manning differs mainly in which object/perspective is assigned to the roles, so preserving it as a mode removes a human organizational distinction without removing adversarial scientific reasoning.

tactics.desc: Characterize what blocks a research target: readiness dimensions, obstacles, bottlenecks, resource gaps, causal constraints, dependencies, conflicts, removability, and mitigation pathways. Depth selects lightweight triage, readiness assessment, or causal/TOC-style constraint analysis.
tactics.why: All three answer the same scientific control question—what prevents this research target from succeeding and what changes would remove the blocker—at different depths and object scopes. Quantitative resource gaps and causal conflict analysis remain optional operators inside the common tactic.

tactics.desc: Generate testable hypotheses from theory, empirical regularity, anomaly, or explicit explanatory competition. Deductive, inductive, abductive, and competing-hypothesis generation are modes; discriminating predictions and comparison are activated in competing mode.
tactics.why: Competing-hypothesis construction is not a separate orchestration kernel: it is hypothesis generation with an additional discriminating-prediction/comparison branch. Preserve that branch as a mode rather than a second Tactic.

tactics.desc: Gate a hypothesis on falsifiability, operational definition, and boundary conditions; can be entered from any hypothesis-generation path.
Convert a hypothesis into a precise research question with fit-for-purpose framework, scope, feasibility, and success criteria.
Decompose a complex RQ into MECE subquestions, map dependencies, and schedule the answering order.
Test whether an apparent gap is real, persistent, and not an evidence-acquisition artifact. Tool choice is left to the host AI.
Move from symptoms to causal structure using complementary root-cause representations and causal-validity checks.
Surface load-bearing assumptions, classify vulnerability, challenge or perturb them, and re-check causal logic.
Generate plausible model variants and test whether conclusions converge across assumption/model choices.
Quantify which parameters, assumptions, interactions, or uncertainties dominate the conclusion; select Morris/Sobol/perturbation/Monte-Carlo as modes.

Change the problem representation when the current frame is limiting: dominant-frame escape, stakeholder/worldview rotation, forced perspective shifts, dialectical/polarity reframing, or abstraction/scope shifts.
tactics.why: The restored forced-perspective tactic shared the same target, perspective-set, and rotation transformation as problem reframing. The creative follow-on is a jump choice, not a separate reframing algorithm.

tactics.desc: Map attack surfaces, generate attack vectors, execute probes, and aggregate weaknesses into a resilience picture.
Enumerate failure modes, trace cause-mode-effect chains, score risk, design mitigations, and re-evaluate residual risk.
Intervene on factors, construct counterfactual worlds, test necessity/sufficiency, and identify load-bearing causal factors.
Negate claims, derive consequences, search contradictions/counterexamples, then refine scope rather than merely defend the original wording.
Abstract relational structure from source domains, map it to the target, validate depth, and instantiate transferable mechanisms.

Break fixation by surfacing assumptions and applying deliberate provocation modes (reversal, negation, random entry, exaggeration, extreme/zero-resource constraint, distortion), then extract constructive movement and synthesize candidate directions.
tactics.why: Random-entry and extreme-constraint SOPs restored during closure are already explicit modes of the canonical generate-provocation transform; keeping them as separate primitives double-counted the same operation.

tactics.desc: Decompose a system and apply component/function transformations such as remove, substitute, combine, redistribute, divide, or reverse.
Map known methods against problem/parameter space and generate candidates from uncovered intersections. Acquisition mechanism is runtime-selected.
Select informative comparison pairs, execute judgments, update ratings, and audit coherence until ranking resolution is sufficient.

Map disagreement, iterate evidence/argument refinement, and terminate with an output contract containing stable consensus, unresolved disagreements, confidence/probabilities, and threshold/stop rationale.
Formalize objectives/constraints, construct a Pareto frontier, stress across scenarios, and select a robust portfolio.
Map candidate research fields or subfields, their maturity, competition, entry barriers, and opportunity structure. Evidence/tool acquisition is host-selected.
Turn a research direction into an AND/OR goal DAG with testable leaves, dependency structure, and feasibility annotations.
Build a reproducible literature evidence base. Scoping, systematic, deep, narrative, and snowball are execution modes selected from intent and budget, not separate strategy nodes.
Map a patent landscape using families, classifications, assignees, filing dynamics, quality, and technical-domain coverage without prescribing a patent provider.
Assess novelty/prior art and claim scope by decomposing claims, tracing relevant families, and checking status/provenance.
Map protected feature combinations and identify technically meaningful, plausibly unprotected white space.
Treat benchmarks as scientific measurement instruments: audit construct validity, contamination, metric pathology, coverage, leaderboard dynamics, and protocol drift.
Design or execute a quantitative evidence synthesis with pairwise/network/cumulative/heterogeneity/bias modes while preserving study-level quality and sensitivity logic.
Establish a fair empirical baseline by inventorying methods, extracting comparable performance, normalizing conditions/compute, checking discrepancies, and estimating progress/headroom.
Construct a tool-independent domain ontology: scope the domain, atomize concepts, type relations, build hierarchy, audit consistency, detect gaps, and refine confidence.
Construct and validate an explicit causal model with measurable variables, mechanism edges, evidence links, feedback loops, interventions, counterevidence, and confidence.
Atomize claims, expose premises and counterclaims, attach evidence/defeaters, score claim strength, and construct an inspectable argument graph independent of storage format.
Translate a falsifiable hypothesis into a statistically defensible experiment. Factorial, ablation, comparison, scaling, and robustness designs are modes, not strategy nodes.
Construct and compare plausible future/competitive/temporal/stress scenarios and test whether the research path remains robust across them.
Interpret completed experimental outputs after host/runtime execution using pre-declared statistical tests, effect/uncertainty estimates, reproducibility checks, and calibrated synthesis.

Model the research system from stakeholder and boundary perspectives: define what is inside/outside the system, identify stakeholder jobs and stakes, classify salience, and expose conflicts that alter problem framing or feasibility.
tactics.why: Pass 6 retained generic perspective/reframing ideas but lost stakeholder-specific system-boundary and salience semantics. Those affect what counts as the problem, evidence, and feasible intervention, so they require a dedicated tactic.

tactics.desc: Turn a design or research contradiction into targeted transformations using inventive-principle and separation reasoning, then evaluate whether the transformed configuration resolves the contradiction without creating a worse one.
tactics.why: TRIZ contradiction/separation reasoning is not equivalent to generic component transformation: it explicitly encodes improving-vs-worsening parameters and separation conditions. Restored as a distinct scientific ideation tactic.

tactics.desc: Reframe a problem in biological functional terms, discover organisms/systems solving analogous functions, extract the causal biological strategy, and transfer the mechanism back into the target domain.
tactics.why: Generic analogy preserves mapping but not the biologize→discover→extract-strategy workflow that makes biomimicry operational. The capability is therefore restored as a parameterized domain-transfer tactic.

tactics.desc: Construct multiple input spaces, extract a shared generic space, selectively project structure into a blend, and simulate emergent properties that are not present in either source alone.
tactics.why: Simple combination/enumeration cannot express emergent blended structure. Conceptual blending is restored because its generic-space and selective-projection semantics are genuinely different from morphological search.

tactics.desc: Maintain a diverse population of candidate solutions, mutate/recombine variants, select under explicit fitness and novelty criteria, and iterate while preserving useful niches rather than collapsing prematurely to one winner.
tactics.why: A static combination search does not preserve population dynamics, iterative selection, or diversity pressure. These are the essential semantics of evolutionary ideation and are restored as a tactic.

tactics.desc: Convert a sharp scientific claim into the cheapest decisive falsification program. Steelman the claim into a precise testable form, specify observations/computations that could break it, execute the most informative probes first, and return only BROKEN, CORROBORATED, or UNFALSIFIABLE rather than a resilience score.
tactics.why: The current repository contains a truth-seeking sibling to ordinary red-teaming whose objective function is reversed: cheap falsification rather than survival/hardening. Generic adversarial-deliberation cannot preserve its verdict semantics or unfalsifiability penalty.

tactics.desc: Audit a claimed isomorphism/equivalence by constructing an explicit mapping, testing which structures/operations/invariants are preserved, searching counterexamples, and downgrading the claim to the strongest defensible relation when full isomorphism fails.
tactics.why: Analogy generation and structural mapping are not enough: the old method explicitly falsifies equivalence claims and uses a downgrade ladder from isomorphism to weaker relations.

tactics.desc: Audit whether a validator, benchmark, sandbox, or test can pass by construction because it embeds the same assumptions as the theory it claims to validate. Build a claim×validator-assumption matrix and demand at least one non-circular failure channel.
tactics.why: Validator circularity is a distinct methodological failure: ordinary construct-validity or evidence-independence checks do not expose PASS-by-construction when the test inherits the target theory assumptions.

tactics.desc: Audit claims of independent convergence by tracing shared priors, data, framing, models, prompts, assumptions, or upstream evidence; estimate an effective independent evidence count rather than treating nominal N paths as independent.
tactics.why: The old capability explicitly discounts correlated agreement. Generic consensus and evidence independence do not quantify shared-error structure across convergent reasoning paths.

tactics.desc: Test whether an elegant/simple explanation earns its compression by forbidding alternatives, subsuming independent facts, or making risky predictions, rather than merely relabeling observations with a compact vocabulary.
tactics.why: Simplicity is not automatically evidence. This audit turns elegance into falsifiable methodological criteria and therefore is not equivalent to generic plausibility or scoring.

sops.desc: Normalize heterogeneous gap records into a comparable schema before decision operations.
sops.why: Retain as a dedicated data-contract operation; no strong cross-package duplicate established yet.

sops.desc: Derive explicit evaluation criteria from the research objective and candidate set.
sops.why: Same transform with different downstream schemas; parameterize criterion schema.

sops.desc: Produce a normalized criterion-weight vector using a selected elicitation method.
sops.why: Method changes, contract does not: criteria -> normalized weights + consistency diagnostics.

sops.desc: Aggregate criterion or comparison results into an ordered recommendation under an explicit rule.
sops.why: Shared aggregation transform; output schema and aggregation rule remain parameters.

sops.desc: Identify theories relevant to a gap and characterize their applicability. Evidence acquisition is not prescribed.
sops.why: Scientific semantic operator retained; literature-engine dependency removed.

sops.desc: Identify relevant variables/factors and annotate functional roles.
sops.why: Related but not identical vocabularies; parameterize role ontology (causal variable, factor, design dimension).

sops.desc: Specify direction, functional form, and theoretical basis of relationships among variables.
sops.why: Retain specialized scientific contract.

sops.desc: Determine what observation would falsify a hypothesis and flag unfalsifiable formulations.
sops.why: Core philosophy-level operation; should remain explicit.

sops.desc: Turn abstract variables/constructs into measurable operational definitions.
sops.why: Retain; distinct from identifying variables.

sops.desc: State applicability assumptions, scope, and known boundary conditions.
sops.why: Common scope-contract operation; refinement logic remains in its parent tactic.

sops.desc: Generate mechanism-distinct explanations rather than superficial paraphrases.
sops.why: Retain specialized scientific operation.

sops.desc: Construct a prediction that yields different outcomes under competing hypotheses.
sops.why: Distinct scientific operation; do not collapse into generic prediction.

sops.desc: Build an explicit comparison matrix over hypotheses, predictions, and evidence.
sops.why: Retain structured comparison contract.

sops.desc: Select and instantiate a research-question schema appropriate to study type.
sops.why: Strong fixed family: framework choice plus filling a typed schema. Framework is a parameter, not five SOPs.

sops.desc: Audit a research question for scope and FINER-style quality; return targeted repairs.
sops.why: Safe as a composite SOP because these checks are repeatedly used as one refinement gate.

sops.desc: Decompose a research question into MECE subquestions with coverage and independence arguments.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Construct a dependency graph and identify cycles, critical paths, and parallelizable branches.
sops.why: Same graph transform across question decomposition and system ablation; input entity type is a parameter.

sops.desc: Topologically sequence dependent work while prioritizing fail-fast/high-risk branches.
sops.why: Retain as scientific planning primitive; runtime may execute it however it chooses.

sops.desc: Seek independent evidence channels sufficient to determine whether a finding/gap is source-specific. No database/provider is named.
sops.why: Preserve epistemic purpose, remove provider-specific implementation.

sops.desc: Distinguish a real knowledge gap from search failure, already-resolved questions, or intrinsically unanswerable formulations.
sops.why: Unique gap epistemology operator.

sops.desc: Enumerate explicit and implicit assumptions in a claim, model, method, decision, or design.
sops.why: Very strong canonical merge: same transform, different naming and local taxonomy.

sops.desc: Classify assumptions by load-bearing importance and vulnerability.
sops.why: Keep; adds a specific decision representation beyond extraction.

sops.desc: Construct a strong countercase or alternative to an assumption and assess consequence if it fails.
sops.why: Parameterized merge around target type and challenge mode.

sops.desc: Apply a controlled change to an assumption, factor, component, parameter, or condition and record response.
sops.why: High-value AI-native primitive. Removal, negation, and numeric variation are modes with explicit semantics.

sops.desc: Audit a causal relation for clarity, existence, sufficiency, and logical completeness using CLR-style checks.
sops.why: Method-specific and rigorous; retain.

sops.desc: Generate a plausible model variant by relaxing, replacing, or generalizing assumptions.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Identify factors/assumptions/uncertainties whose change most strongly controls the conclusion.
sops.why: Common influence-identification contract; keep metric and factor ontology configurable.

sops.desc: Locate the point or region where performance/validity changes regime or the claim flips.
sops.why: Canonical endpoint of perturbation workflows.

sops.desc: Synthesize multi-axis breakpoints into a multidimensional statement of where a claim/method remains valid.
sops.why: Direct duplicate across packages; merge is high confidence.

sops.desc: Iteratively ask why, evidence-checking each causal step, to move from symptom toward root cause.
sops.why: Retain method-specific behavior.

sops.desc: Build an Ishikawa-style causal decomposition across relevant cause families.
sops.why: Retain method-specific representation.

sops.desc: Build a sufficient-cause Current Reality Tree linking undesirable effects to a small root set.
sops.why: Retain method-specific causal logic.

sops.desc: Identify the dominant framing/paradigm or governing variable constraining the current problem representation.
sops.why: Parameterized merge: all surface the latent frame that constrains search.

sops.desc: Construct the strongest structured attack on a claim/artifact, grounded in explicit reasons/evidence.
sops.why: Role implementation disappears; critique is the cognitive operation.

sops.desc: Construct the strongest defensible case while acknowledging valid weaknesses.
sops.why: Strong cross-package duplicate.

sops.desc: Evaluate competing arguments against stated criteria and produce a reasoned verdict with uncertainty.
sops.why: Strong cross-package duplicate; no agent topology required.

sops.desc: Probe responses for inconsistency, logic gaps, and unsupported claims.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Enumerate attackable dimensions of an artifact and rate exposure/accessibility.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Generate a concrete executable attack/probe against a chosen threat surface.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Execute one test/attack and record outcome, evidence, and severity. Tool use is runtime-selected.
sops.why: Retain scientific test semantics; remove subagent/tool binding.

sops.desc: Convert functions/process steps/scenarios into explicit failure modes.
sops.why: Retain FMEA semantics.

sops.desc: Build multi-level cause -> failure mode -> effect chains and identify cascades/shared roots.
old: deep-insight/failure-clustering (mechanism grouping adjacent, not fully merged)
sops.why: Core chain construction retained; clustering remains parent logic.

sops.desc: Score severity, occurrence, detectability, and derive action priority for a failure mode.
sops.why: Strong fixed composition. These four are almost always consumed as one FMEA scoring unit; pin into one SOP.

sops.desc: Construct the minimally or explicitly intervened counterfactual world required by the parent analysis.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Produce a scope-preserving logical negation of a claim or assumption.
sops.why: Canonical logical operation; tactic decides why the negation is being used.

sops.desc: Trace logically valid consequences from an altered premise, provocation, or negated claim.
sops.why: Shared consequence propagation; rigor mode can be deductive vs exploratory.

sops.desc: Repair a claim via scope narrowing, lemma incorporation, or decomposition while preserving explanatory power.
sops.why: Retain as Lakatos-style repair operation, not generic editing.

sops.desc: Remove domain surface details to expose transferable relational/mechanistic structure at a chosen abstraction level.
sops.why: Abstraction level is a parameter; all share concrete -> relational representation.

sops.desc: Map source structure/relations/functions to target structure and annotate match quality.
sops.why: Combine mapping plus match-quality annotation; source domain is parameterized.

sops.desc: Turn an abstract transferred principle into a concrete target-domain design/mechanism.
sops.why: Strong shared source: abstract connection -> concrete candidate.

sops.desc: Construct combinations across dimensions/values without prematurely judging them.
sops.why: Strong combinatorial primitive; representation can be matrix or stream.

sops.desc: Evaluate logical/empirical/normative compatibility of a candidate combination and prune invalid regions.
sops.why: All implement consistency pruning over generated combinations.

sops.desc: Generate a deliberate pattern-breaking perturbation: PO, reversal, negation, random stimulus, exaggeration, or distortion.
sops.why: Stimulus mode becomes a parameter. Preserve whether randomness is required.

sops.desc: Convert an initially absurd/destructive provocation into concrete useful directions.
sops.why: Strong shared movement transform.

sops.desc: Decompose a system into components/functions and record dependencies relevant to transformation.
sops.why: Same decomposition backbone; parent specifies design vs failure-analysis purpose.

sops.desc: Apply an explicit structural/function operator such as remove, substitute, combine, divide, redirect, redistribute, or reverse.
sops.why: Operator is data. Keep highly specialized operators as named modes when their preconditions matter.

sops.desc: Integrate generated fragments into a coherent candidate with mechanism, provenance, and next-test hooks.
sops.why: Candidate merge only if output schema is made explicit. Parent tactic supplies provenance fields and acceptance contract.

sops.desc: Identify Pareto-dominated and non-dominated alternatives under strict dominance.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Define a justified minimum acceptable threshold for each non-compensatory criterion.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Eliminate alternatives that violate any hard threshold and report the exact violation.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Select the next comparison pair to maximize expected information gain.
sops.why: Retain active-comparison primitive.

sops.desc: Execute one pairwise comparison under a specified criterion/model and return winner, confidence, and reasons.
sops.why: Strong shared pairwise judgment contract.

sops.desc: Audit pairwise/ranking coherence and identify inconsistent cycles/triads.
sops.why: Shared consistency audit; metric can vary.

sops.desc: Represent where perspectives/arguments agree, disagree, and why.
sops.why: Same cross-view divergence mapping; consensus thresholds become parameters.

sops.desc: Run one structured revision round that updates arguments/evidence rather than merely averaging opinions.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Assess one readiness dimension against explicit anchors/evidence.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Identify the limiting dimension or dependency currently constraining progress.
sops.why: Common limiting-factor operation; parent defines domain.

sops.desc: Classify constraints as hard, soft, or assumption-like after explicit identification.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Estimate whether and at what cost a constraint can be removed or relaxed.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Formalize objectives, constraints, and tradeoff preferences for optimization.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Generate a non-dominated frontier for a multi-objective candidate/portfolio problem.
sops.why: Retain algorithmic contract; solver implementation is runtime/tool choice.

sops.desc: Select a preferred frontier point/portfolio and state the sacrificed alternatives/tradeoffs.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Construct a scenario across key uncertainties with explicit assumptions and plausibility. Modes include baseline/narrative, counterfactual, and extreme-but-plausible worst-case with breaking point, failure cascade, recovery assumptions, and distinguishing observables.
sops.why: Worst-case construction is preserved as a strict scenario mode with additional required fields, rather than a separate primitive.

sops.desc: Generate diverse candidate research fields/subfields consistent with current context while permitting deliberate boundary-crossing.
sops.why: Subagent wrapper removed; generative operator retained.

sops.desc: Summarize candidate fields by maturity, competition, entry barrier, tractability, and publication/opportunity structure.
sops.why: Evidence source is external; synthesis contract remains.

sops.desc: Enumerate obstacles that block a target goal/direction, with type, evidence, and blocking relation.
sops.why: Safe cross-package merge; both map blockers to a goal.

sops.desc: Formalize a research goal as an outcome, desired effect, and explicit constraints.
sops.why: Retain semantic contract; confirmation is optional runtime interaction.

sops.desc: Recursively decompose a goal into an AND/OR DAG whose leaves are executable or testable subgoals.
sops.why: KAOS-style decomposition is distinct and useful.

sops.desc: Check leaf specificity, testability, coverage of the parent goal, logical completeness, and dependency consistency.
sops.why: Human approval removed; validation remains.

sops.desc: Cross-check goal branches against resources, obstacles, and timeline; label feasible/stretch/infeasible and propose OR alternatives.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Compress the goal structure and intentionality into a specific, ambitious, achievable one-sentence research North Star.
sops.why: Retain final semantic transformation.

sops.desc: Define research questions, evidence scope, queries/concepts, inclusion/exclusion rules, provenance requirements, and stopping evidence for an acquisition task.
sops.why: Tool-independent protocol replaces provider-specific search instructions.

sops.desc: Select and rank high-information seed sources for iterative evidence expansion using quality, recency, relevance, and network position.
sops.why: Retain methodological seed selection; acquisition mechanism is external.

sops.desc: Cluster an evidence corpus by theme, method, chronology, mechanism, or another declared schema.
sops.why: Canonical corpus organization transform.

sops.desc: Estimate marginal information gain of new evidence batches relative to the current corpus and classify continuing/near-saturation/saturated.
sops.why: Keep scientific saturation; unlike generic budget stopping, this uses evidence novelty.

sops.desc: Trace priority, family membership, forward/backward citations, and continuation relationships until relevant family structure stabilizes.
sops.why: Patent-specific semantic operation retained.

sops.desc: Traverse IPC/CPC-like classification neighborhoods to expand or delimit a technical patent domain.
sops.why: Provider independent; taxonomy navigation retained.

sops.desc: Parse independent/dependent claim structure, extract elements, and map claim features to technical functions/domains.
sops.why: Merge tactic and leaf operation into one bounded primitive contract.

sops.desc: Classify observed patent/legal status and flag uncertainty or jurisdiction dependence.
sops.why: Retain; data access is external.

sops.desc: Decompose an evaluation metric into rewarded signals, aggregation choices, polarity, ceiling effects, and Goodhart vulnerabilities.
sops.why: Distinct measurement-science operation.

sops.desc: Audit train/test leakage, memorization artifacts, temporal leakage, and disclosure pathways that can invalidate evaluation.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Assess whether a benchmark measures its claimed capability using content, convergent, discriminant, and confound analysis.
sops.why: Retain psychometric contract.

sops.desc: Analyze leaderboard score distributions, compression/saturation, anomalies, selective reporting, and regime shifts.
sops.why: Retain benchmark-dynamics semantics.

sops.desc: Extract evaluation-protocol elements from a source and mark unstated or ambiguous parameters.
sops.why: Retain source-to-protocol transform.

sops.desc: Build a protocol-difference matrix and estimate which differences can materially change measured performance.
sops.why: Compress old tactic to SOP because its bounded transform is stable and usually nested in benchmark audit.

sops.desc: Instantiate a typed evidence question schema such as PICO/PECO for quantitative synthesis.
sops.why: Reuse schema-instantiation principle; meta-analysis requires outcome/comparator details.

sops.desc: Define study inclusion/exclusion criteria and explicit rules for borderline cases.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Choose effect-size estimands and required conversions/calculation rules appropriate to the outcomes and design.
sops.why: Retain statistical semantics.

sops.desc: Define a structured extraction form, field semantics, coding rules, and missing-data handling for evidence synthesis.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Identify clinical, methodological, and statistical heterogeneity sources and prioritize subgroup/meta-regression/outlier investigation.
sops.why: Strategy collapses into one bounded analysis primitive inside meta-analysis tactic.

sops.desc: Assess or plan tests for publication/reporting/time-lag/citation/language bias using appropriate diagnostics.
sops.why: Collapse mode wrapper into primitive.

sops.desc: Construct a network-meta-analysis evidence graph and evaluate connectivity/transitivity prerequisites.
sops.why: Retain NMA-specific operation.

sops.desc: Detect material score discrepancies for the same method/task across sources and propose likely explanatory condition differences.
sops.why: Collapse wrapper into stable comparison primitive.

sops.desc: Estimate practical/human/theoretical ceilings and remaining performance headroom under stated assumptions.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Define ontology/model scope, inclusion boundaries, granularity, and intended use before structural extraction.
sops.why: Retain domain-bounding semantics.

sops.desc: Extract candidate concepts from evidence with explicit source provenance and precision/recall posture.
sops.why: Remove vault/web implementation; retain concept discovery.

sops.desc: Decompose compound concepts into atomic, non-overlapping concepts while preserving parent/part relationships.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Classify relations among entities using an explicit relation ontology and state evidence/assumptions for the type.
sops.why: Storage edge creation removed; semantic relation typing retained.

sops.desc: Construct an acyclic is-a/part-of/instance-of hierarchy with explicit roots, depth, and transitivity constraints.
sops.why: Old tactic compresses to SOP inside ontology construction.

sops.desc: Detect cycles, contradictions, orphans, type violations, and structural incoherence in a knowledge model.
sops.why: Stable graph-audit transform; no vault tooling required.

sops.desc: Update confidence in a concept, relation, claim, or model component from new supporting/contradicting evidence with explicit rationale.
sops.why: Canonical evidence-to-confidence transform.

sops.desc: Represent a directed mechanism edge with pathway, sign/direction, assumptions, falsifier, strength, and evidence provenance.
sops.why: Storage write removed; causal representation retained.

sops.desc: Attach supporting or contradicting evidence to a specific claim/relation with quality, directness, and independence metadata.
sops.why: Direct semantic duplicate across causal/argument workflows.

sops.desc: Detect and characterize reinforcing/balancing feedback loops, participating variables, delays, and possible breakpoints.
sops.why: Storage page creation removed.

sops.desc: Trace ordered causal chains including intermediate nodes, branches, and loops with explicit because/mechanism links.
sops.why: High-confidence cross-package merge.

sops.desc: Apply an intervention/do-style graph modification and propagate predicted directional effects while recording assumptions.
sops.why: Artifact write removed; causal intervention retained.

sops.desc: Test candidate dimensions pairwise for independence/redundancy; merge covarying axes and remove non-informative axes.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Decompose a compound position into atomic, independently challengeable/falsifiable claims and expose implicit assumptions.
sops.why: Storage page creation removed; atomicity operation retained.

sops.desc: Construct a counterclaim, identify its target claim, contradiction type, assumptions, and supporting evidence requirements.
sops.why: Remove page/write semantics.

sops.desc: Construct a balanced/randomized/orthogonal experimental design matrix appropriate to the chosen design mode.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Define primary/secondary metrics, estimands, directionality, uncertainty reporting, and decision thresholds before analysis.
sops.why: Retain and generalize beyond significance threshold.

sops.desc: Estimate sample/repetition requirements from detectable effect, uncertainty, power/precision target, and design structure.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Select fair SOTA/simple/oracle/control baselines with provenance and rationale matched to the experimental claim.
sops.why: Retain; evidence retrieval external.

sops.desc: Map system structure into ablatable units, dependencies, legal removal/replacement operations, and expected contribution hypotheses.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Identify randomness sources and define seed/repetition/propagation rules sufficient for the intended reproducibility level.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Specify environment variables that materially affect interpretation or reproducibility: hardware, software, data, configuration, and versioning.
sops.why: Semantic reproducibility requirement retained; no execution platform assumed.

sops.desc: Select statistical inference/estimation method from design, distribution, sample size, pairing, multiplicity, and decision objective.
sops.why: Old tactic is a bounded selection transform; compress to SOP.

sops.desc: Define exact/statistical/conceptual reproduction target and the controls needed to test it.
sops.why: Compress to SOP; host runtime decides how reruns are executed.

sops.desc: Given cost per run and resource budget, choose the most information-efficient feasible design while preserving essential validity constraints.
sops.why: Scientific design optimization retained; generic budget bookkeeping remains runtime.

sops.desc: List observable undesirable effects with evidence and severity as starting points for constraint/root-cause analysis.
sops.why: Retain TOC semantic operation.

sops.desc: Represent a core constraint conflict in an Evaporating-Cloud-like structure with explicit assumptions on every dependency.
sops.why: Retain method-specific representation.

sops.desc: Quantify resource demand, available supply, gap, severity, and uncertainty for a research/experiment plan.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Identify the longest/limiting dependency path while accounting for resource contention and convergence points.
sops.why: Retain; overlaps dependency graph but adds resource contention.

sops.desc: Project the downstream consequences of a proposed constraint-breaking intervention and detect new undesirable effects.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Identify high-impact/high-uncertainty drivers and rank them for scenario construction.
sops.why: PESTEL is an optional mode, not hard dependency.

sops.desc: Predict plausible competitor research moves, timing, and preemption/priority risk with explicit assumptions.
sops.why: Retain.

sops.desc: Apply the pre-declared statistical/estimation procedure and report effect size, uncertainty, model checks, and decision-relevant interpretation.
sops.why: Retain; calculation implementation can use any available tool.

sops.desc: Assess reproducibility across reruns/replications using the predeclared reproducibility target and suitable agreement/variance metrics.
sops.why: Execution of reruns is runtime; assessment is scientific cognition.

sops.desc: Perturb a specified input, assumption, model choice, analysis choice, or weight and measure sensitivity of a specified output; report convergence/instability, unstable regions, and dominant drivers.
sops.why: Same core transform: perturb inputs -> recompute/compare output -> quantify instability. Target/output metric becomes a parameter.

sops.desc: Identify approximately independent dimensions/axes that span the relevant problem, design, or validity space and define their semantics.
sops.why: Both convert an unstructured space into named axes; downstream enumeration/exploration is separate.

sops.desc: Enumerate meaningful values/levels for a dimension or factor. Mode controls representative, experimental, boundary, pathological, or adversarial coverage.
sops.why: Same axis -> value-set transform. Experimental spacing and extreme/adversarial generation are modes with explicit constraints.

sops.desc: Design an intervention that prevents, detects, responds to, removes, or relaxes a failure mode/constraint; state residual risk and validation evidence.
sops.why: Both create a response path to a limiting condition. Intervention mode is parameterized.

sops.desc: Evaluate a fixed candidate, research path, or portfolio under one explicit scenario using stable criteria and return impact, tradeoffs, and failure triggers.
sops.why: Directly equivalent scenario-conditioned evaluation contracts across convergence and experiment planning.

sops.desc: Analyze an ordered temporal trajectory, including persistence/narrowing/widening tests, regime changes, inflection points, and optional extrapolation with uncertainty. Entity type, window, and forecast mode are parameters.
sops.why: Same time-indexed evidence -> trend/regime/forecast transform; patent filings, SOTA progress, and research timelines are schemas.

sops.desc: Given an explicit coverage representation (matrix, graph, taxonomy, IP feature space), identify absent, thin, disconnected, or weakly covered regions and characterize why they matter.
sops.why: Same negative-space operation over different representations; representation type is a parameter.

sops.desc: Audit a study against an appropriate methodological-quality and risk-of-bias rubric; return domain-level judgments, evidence, and overall confidence.
sops.why: Both are study-level methodological validity audits. RoB2/ROBINS-I/etc. are rubric parameters rather than separate cognitive operations.

sops.desc: Audit whether a research/evaluation artifact reports the information needed for interpretation and reproduction, using a domain-appropriate checklist.
sops.why: Same checklist-based completeness audit; benchmark documentation and paper reproducibility use different rubrics.

sops.desc: Detect an explicit contradiction in logical derivations, claims, or evidence relations; classify whether it is formal, empirical, scope-dependent, or unresolved.
sops.why: Both detect incompatible propositions/evidence. Contradiction type and resolution policy are parameters.

sops.desc: Extract causal structure from source material at requested granularity: individual causal claims, ordered mechanism chains, mediators, assumptions, and stated boundary conditions.
sops.why: Same source -> causal representation operation; granularity distinguishes pair extraction from mechanism-chain extraction.

sops.desc: Map a set of methods/assets/evidence items against a typed problem, capability, condition, or design space to expose redundancy and coverage structure.
sops.why: Both build an item x capability/problem coverage representation before gap detection.

sops.desc: Resolve aliases and near-duplicates into canonical entities while preserving provenance and rejecting false merges; entity schema is configurable.
sops.why: Same identity-resolution transform for concepts and organizations/assignees.

sops.desc: Extract a schema-declared evidence record from a source, including methods, datasets, metrics/results, conditions, limitations, provenance, and explicitly missing/ambiguous fields.
sops.why: Pass 4 provenance already duplicated score-extraction and condition-cataloging across these nodes. Performance records and evaluation conditions are typed projections of one schema-guided evidence-extraction transform.

sops.desc: Normalize heterogeneous values onto a declared comparison scale while preserving direction, units, uncertainty, and the transformation rule. The normalized object may be criterion scores, resource budgets, or another comparable quantity.
sops.why: Both operations transform heterogeneous numeric evidence into a comparable scale. Efficiency/Pareto interpretation remains a separate call to check-dominance rather than being hidden inside normalization.

sops.desc: Score a typed object against an explicit rubric with evidence, uncertainty, and rationale. The parent tactic supplies the object schema and rubric (candidate, gap, claim, obstacle, etc.).
sops.why: All four nodes perform rubric-conditioned evidence-backed scoring. Their scientific content lies in the rubric supplied by the tactic, not in four separate scoring mechanics. Formula-specific operators such as FMEA risk remain specialized.

sops.desc: Build a structured inventory of externally established reference items under a parent-specified schema, preserving applicability/status, key attributes, limitations, and provenance. Typical schemas include benchmark or known-solution/method family.
sops.why: Both operations catalog external reference items with typed metadata and provenance. Research-resource elicitation remains separate because it inventories the agent/project's available resources, not external evidence objects.

sops.desc: Select most-likely, least-likely, or otherwise inference-maximizing cases that can decisively support/refute a claim under explicit case-selection logic.
sops.why: Pass 5 retained boundary probing but lost Flyvbjerg-style critical-case selection. This is a distinct inferential operation, not generic extreme-value generation.

sops.desc: Update candidate latent ratings and uncertainty from sequential pairwise outcomes using an explicitly chosen Bradley-Terry/Elo/Glicko/TrueSkill-style update model.
sops.why: Pass 5 pairwise-ranking described online rating updates but had no operator that actually updates a rating state.

sops.desc: Aggregate and iteratively recalibrate probabilistic forecasts, preserving uncertainty, calibration evidence, and unresolved forecaster disagreement.
sops.why: Consensus iteration alone does not preserve the probability-calibration semantics of futures/forecast Delphi.

sops.desc: Quantify portfolio diversity/coverage across declared feature, mechanism, domain, or failure-mode dimensions and expose concentration/niche collapse.
sops.why: Pareto optimality does not by itself preserve the MAP-Elites/niche-coverage capability of the old portfolio workflow.

sops.desc: Evaluate the value of staging, deferral, reversible commitment, and information-gathering options under uncertainty; return decision-relevant option value and trigger conditions.
sops.why: Dependency sequencing alone does not preserve the Real-Options component of the old temporal portfolio strategy.

sops.desc: Define and challenge the system boundary: what actors, processes, externalities, timescales, and value assumptions are included or excluded.
sops.why: System-boundary critique changes the problem definition itself; generic scope specification does not preserve the normative inclusion/exclusion audit.

sops.desc: Represent stakeholder jobs, desired outcomes, pains, gains, dependencies, and conflicts relevant to the research target.
sops.why: JTBD-style functional demand is distinct from merely listing actors.

sops.desc: Classify stakeholder salience using power, legitimacy, urgency, dependency, or a supplied salience schema.
sops.why: Stakeholder salience is a typed prioritization contract and was missing after compression.

sops.desc: Construct an explicit set of scientifically relevant viewpoints, roles, worldviews, stakeholder positions, or epistemic lenses to apply to the same object.
sops.why: Multiple old families independently required explicit viewpoint construction. This is a reusable basis operator.

sops.desc: Apply one perspective at a time to reinterpret the same target while holding the underlying evidence/object fixed; record changed assumptions, objectives, risks, and opportunities.
sops.why: Perspective rotation is a transformation of the observer/frame and is reusable across insight, ideation, and adversarial review.

sops.desc: Identify paired parameters or requirements where improving one worsens another, and distinguish technical from physical contradictions.
sops.why: Needed to preserve TRIZ-specific contradiction semantics.

sops.desc: Select one or more inventive principles appropriate to a contradiction or transformation objective and state why each principle applies.
sops.why: Generic transform-component does not encode targeted principle selection.

sops.desc: Resolve a physical contradiction by separating conflicting requirements in time, space, scale, condition, or system level.
sops.why: Separation reasoning is an irreducible TRIZ operation.

sops.desc: Translate a target problem from implementation language into biological function/constraint language suitable for biological analogy search.
sops.why: This reframing contract is what makes biomimicry search mechanism-directed rather than keyword-directed.

sops.desc: Identify biological systems that achieve the target function under comparable constraints, without assuming surface similarity.
sops.why: Biological analog discovery uses function/constraint matching, distinct from generic analogy generation.

sops.desc: Extract the causal strategy/mechanism by which a biological analog achieves its function, including boundary conditions and trade-offs.
sops.why: Preserves causal transfer rather than superficial inspiration.

sops.desc: Define the structured input spaces for conceptual blending: entities, relations, goals, constraints, and salient dynamics in each source.
sops.why: Required before selective projection into a blend.

sops.desc: Infer the shared abstract relational structure that is common across conceptual-blend input spaces.
sops.why: Generic space is not equivalent to simply finding an analogy because it mediates multi-source blending.

sops.desc: Project selected structures into a candidate blend and reason through properties, affordances, contradictions, or mechanisms that emerge only in the blend.
sops.why: Emergent property search is the capability that would be lost if conceptual blending were reduced to combination enumeration.

sops.desc: Generate controlled variants of a solution population through mutation/recombination operators while retaining lineage and changed dimensions.
sops.why: Population variation has stateful lineage semantics absent from one-shot ideation.

sops.desc: Select candidate variants under fitness, novelty, constraint, and diversity criteria while avoiding premature population collapse.
sops.why: Evolutionary selection differs from final MCDA because it is an iterative population update.

sops.desc: Expand a target goal into progressively broader concepts and alternative routes, then descend into new concrete approaches.
sops.why: Concept-fan expansion is a structured divergence operator.

sops.desc: Classify a candidate research gap by type (evidence, method, mechanism, population, theory, measurement, contradiction, boundary, translation, etc.) and record implications for next actions.
sops.why: Pass 6 validated and ranked gaps but had lost the typed gap diagnosis that determines how a gap should be attacked.

sops.desc: Estimate global main effects and interactions across uncertain inputs using screening/decomposition methods such as Morris→Sobol or an equivalent supplied method.
sops.why: Local perturbation sensitivity is not equivalent to global variance decomposition with interaction attribution.

sops.desc: Propagate input/parameter uncertainty through a model or reasoning chain to estimate output distributions, tail behavior, and uncertainty contributions.
sops.why: A single sensitivity score does not preserve distributional uncertainty propagation.

sops.desc: Estimate the value of resolving uncertainty (e.g., EVPI/EVSI or qualitative equivalent) to prioritize which unknowns justify further evidence or experiments.
sops.why: Decision sensitivity needs an explicit information-value contract, not only perturbation response.

sops.desc: Assess whether the problem is tame, complex, or wicked by examining stakeholder disagreement, moving boundaries, feedback, value conflict, and absence of a stable stopping rule.
sops.why: Wickedness changes which research workflow is valid; it cannot be inferred from generic obstacle severity alone.

sops.desc: Reframe a problem around functioning exceptions, existing strengths, positive deviance, and conditions under which desired behavior already occurs.
sops.why: Preserves a distinct reframing direction that searches for generative exceptions rather than failure causes.

sops.desc: Analyze how conclusions/performance change across scale and identify regime shifts, saturation, power-law/log-law behavior, or frontier transitions.
sops.why: Scale-dependent validity is more specific than generic temporal/boundary perturbation.

sops.desc: Track confidence in competing claims/roles across adversarial rounds and update confidence only when evidence or argument quality warrants it.
sops.why: Debate without explicit calibration can generate rhetorical escalation rather than epistemic updating.

sops.desc: Trace downstream claims, methods, and conclusions that fail when a selected assumption is invalidated; distinguish local from cascading failure.
sops.why: Generic assumption challenge does not encode propagation of failure through dependent claims.

sops.desc: Search for the smallest change to variables/assumptions/conditions that flips a target conclusion, decision, or causal claim.
sops.why: Minimal-flip search is an optimization objective distinct from arbitrary counterfactual generation.

sops.desc: Test whether a proposed cause/mechanism is necessary and/or sufficient under controlled counterfactual or intervention comparisons.
sops.why: Necessity/sufficiency semantics are not preserved by generic causal-link validation alone.

sops.desc: Re-run the relevant failure/adversarial test after a mitigation and verify that risk actually decreases without unacceptable new failure modes.
sops.why: Designing a mitigation is not equivalent to validating it.

sops.desc: Expand an evidence set through backward/forward citation chaining and terminate using explicit relevance/saturation criteria, independent of the retrieval tool used.
sops.why: This preserves a scientific evidence-discovery method while remaining completely tool/MCP agnostic.

sops.desc: Apply explicit staged inclusion/exclusion screening (title/abstract/full evidence or equivalent) with reasons and auditability.
sops.why: Systematic review screening is a methodological operator, not search-tool infrastructure.

sops.desc: Update a cumulative evidence estimate/order as new studies or evidence blocks arrive and detect when inference changes materially over time.
sops.why: Static meta-analysis does not preserve sequential evidence accumulation.

sops.desc: Analyze patent citation/family relationships to identify central prior art, technological lineage, clusters, bridge patents, and citation anomalies.
sops.why: Patent citation topology is not recoverable from family tracing alone.

sops.desc: Probe whether benchmark performance can be explained by shortcuts, artifacts, leakage, annotation cues, metric gaming, or non-target capabilities.
sops.why: Contamination and construct-validity audits do not fully cover active artifact/shortcut probing.

sops.desc: Apply explicit GO / HOLD / RECYCLE / KILL (or supplied) stage-gate criteria with evidence thresholds and next-step conditions.
sops.why: Generic readiness scoring does not preserve staged decision semantics.

sops.desc: Precisely characterize an anomaly by contrasting observation with expectation, quantifying deviation where possible, recording conditions, and excluding obvious/trivial explanations before generating hypotheses.
sops.why: Pass 7 claimed abductive coverage without an anomaly representation contract; restored as the required starting state for best-explanation reasoning.

sops.desc: Extract a repeatable empirical pattern from observations, state its support and exceptions, and generalize cautiously without importing an unsupported mechanism.
sops.why: Induction is not just abduction with a different mode; it requires an explicit observation→regularity transformation before variable/relationship formulation.

sops.desc: Map a persistent two-pole tension where both poles contain value: upsides/downsides of over-focusing each pole, warning signs, and practices that manage the polarity rather than falsely resolving it.
sops.why: A polarity is an enduring tension, not a contradiction to eliminate. Generic disagreement/conflict operators lose this distinction.

sops.desc: Steelman a claim into its strongest precise, bounded, testable form while making hidden quantifiers, scope, mechanisms, and commitments explicit.
sops.why: Truth-seeking adversarial work starts by making the target easier to genuinely falsify, not by weakening it into something defensible.

sops.desc: Specify a concrete observation, computation, intervention, counterexample, or measurement that would count against the sharpened claim, prioritizing cheap high-information tests.
sops.why: Generic attack-vector generation does not require a probe to have a clear falsification relationship to a scientific claim.

sops.desc: Classify a tested claim as BROKEN, CORROBORATED, or UNFALSIFIABLE based on whether a legitimate falsifier succeeded, failed under adequate power, or cannot be specified/reached.
sops.why: Preserves the reversed truth-seeking objective and makes UNFALSIFIABLE a failure rather than a survival win.

sops.desc: Construct an explicit source↔target mapping over objects, relations, operations, constraints, and invariants for a claimed structural equivalence.
sops.why: A claim of isomorphism requires an explicit mapping, not similarity language.

sops.desc: Test whether the proposed mapping preserves the required relations/operations/invariants and actively search for a minimal counterexample to preservation.
sops.why: Provides the falsification step missing from generic analogy mapping.

sops.desc: When full equivalence fails, downgrade to the strongest defensible relation (e.g. substructure, homomorphism, shared invariant, analogy) and record exactly what ceased to be preserved.
sops.why: Prevents binary keep/reject behavior and preserves the old five-level weakening logic.

sops.desc: Enumerate assumptions embedded in a validator/test/sandbox, including data-generation, measurement, simulator, oracle, metric, initialization, and acceptance assumptions.
sops.why: Required to compare validator assumptions against the theory claims being tested.

sops.desc: Cross-tabulate target theory claims/assumptions against validator assumptions and mark independent, shared, derived-from-target, or unknown dependencies.
sops.why: Makes circularity auditable instead of rhetorical.

sops.desc: Identify cases where the validator is structurally unable to reject the target because acceptance follows from assumptions copied from the target theory or construction process.
sops.why: PASS-by-construction is the key failure mode of circular validation and needs an explicit detector.

sops.desc: Trace supposedly independent evidence/reasoning paths to shared priors, datasets, models, prompts, framings, assumptions, or upstream sources that induce correlated errors.
sops.why: Independent convergence requires independence of error sources, not merely separate output paths.

sops.desc: Estimate an effective number of independent evidence/reasoning paths after discounting dependence/correlation; report nominal N, dependence structure, and N_eff.
sops.why: Preserves the explicit N→N_eff correction absent from generic consensus.

sops.desc: Classify simplicity/compression as earned, weak, or decorative based on whether it forbids alternatives, compresses independent facts, or merely renames/repackages them.
sops.why: Makes the epistemic value of elegance explicit.

sops.desc: Derive a risky/nontrivial prediction uniquely or strongly implied by an explanation and test whether available evidence supports it; distinguish post-hoc accommodation from prospective constraint.
sops.why: A compact theory earns evidential credit when it risks being wrong.

sops.desc: Assess protection breadth, limiting elements, support, overlap, design-around vulnerability, and likely scope uncertainty for a patent claim without making legal conclusions beyond the evidence.
sops.why: Parsing claim syntax and legal status did not preserve the old claim-breadth/vulnerability assessment.

sops.desc: Generate a concrete counterexample candidate that satisfies the target claim's stated scope while violating its conclusion or claimed structural property; record whether exclusion would be principled or ad hoc.
sops.why: Pass 7 retained reductio derivation but had no explicit counterexample-generation operator; capability closure restores it as a reusable falsification primitive.

sops.desc: Collect judgments/rankings from multiple genuinely independent evaluators or perspectives before exposing any peer outputs, preserving ballots and rationale for later social-choice aggregation.
sops.why: Pairwise ranking can aggregate comparisons but did not preserve independent-ballot methodology or contamination control.

sops.desc: Move a scientific object up/down in abstraction or narrow/broaden selected scope dimensions (population, mechanism, context, outcome, timeframe, system boundary) until the representation has useful explanatory and experimental leverage.
sops.why: Both operators vary representational granularity while preserving the underlying research object. Why/How laddering and RQ scope calibration are parameterizations of the same transform.

sops.desc: Aggregate a candidate, strategy, or portfolio across explicit scenarios under a declared robust-decision rule such as worst-case score, minimax regret, maximin, threshold survival, or pivot-trigger analysis.
sops.why: Both operators consume per-scenario outcomes and summarize robustness. Their difference is the aggregation rule, not the scientific transform.
